rows.remaining: Fix check_book_code.sh to match `^\s*```` for both the ignore count and the untagged check, then baseline or un-ignore audit.md:361; include bindings/a2a-protocol-slimrpc/README.md as a doctest in that crate's lib.rs; burn down the 14 rustdoc ignores (most need only hidden preamble lines); correct the two stale comments.

new_findings.finding: `without_tls()` is documented as 'plain HTTP only', but only `build()` honours it. `build_grpc()` ignores `config.tls`: an `https://` endpoint gets TLS from transport/grpc.rs:353-370 (apply_tls), and a bare host:port gets TLS under the default `HttpsExceptLoopback` (builder/mod.rs:444).
new_findings.scenario: A user who calls `.without_tls()` to forbid TLS (e.g. a mesh that encrypts, with a policy of no client TLS) and then `build_grpc()` against a card's `host:port` gRPC address dials TLS anyway.

new_findings.finding: `a2a card <URL>` passes no GlobalOpts: it fetches with `resolve_agent_card(url)` / `fetch_card_from_url(url)`, so `--header`, `--timeout` and `--tenant` are silently ignored, while README:61 says '--header ... Extra header on every request' and the flags are 'Accepted before or after the subcommand'. `card verify` (offline.rs:56-63,85) and discovery for send/stream/task (connect.rs:129-132) do pass them.
new_findings.scenario: An agent whose well-known card sits behind an authenticating gateway: `a2a card https://agent --header Authorization=Bearer ...` gets 401 and the user cannot tell the header was dropped; `--timeout 5` still waits the library's 30 s.

new_findings.finding: Says '`BIND-EQUIV-004` is graded **structurally only** ... Proving each binding *enforces* those schemes identically needs a target configured to require credentials.' The kit has that half (tck/src/equivalence.rs:769+ 'BIND-EQUIV-004, enforcement half', README:62 `--auth-token`) and CI runs it against a secured SUT (.github/workflows/tck.yml:197-218, `SUT_PROFILE=secured` ... `--equivalence --auth-token tck-bind-equiv-004-token`). Should read: 'graded in two runs: the unsecured run checks it structurally (security is declared once, at card level); the secured run (`--auth-token`, tck.yml's secured SUT) checks every binding refuses without the token and with a wrong one, and serves with it.'
new_findings.scenario: A reviewer reading the TCK README concludes enforcement is untested and discounts the BIND-EQUIV-004 grade.

new_findings.finding: STABILITY.md §1 says 'The crates are at `0.15.0` (2026-10-25), the newest release' although 0.15.1 shipped 2026-10-26 and every crate's Cargo.toml is now 0.16.0. It, the rustdoc and the 0.15.0 CHANGELOG say deprecated `sign_agent_card` 'is removed in 0.16.0', yet signing.rs:424 still defines it in the 0.16.0 tree and the [Unreleased] Breaking Changes list does not remove it.
new_findings.scenario: 0.16.0 is tagged as-is: the published docs promise a removal that did not happen (harmless to callers, false on its face), or someone removes it at the last minute without a Breaking Changes entry, which check_release_tree.py would not notice.

new_findings.where: scripts/check_book_code.sh (the `re.findall(r"^```rust[^\n]*\bignore\b", text, re.M)` count and `ln.startswith("```")` fence tracking); book/src/deployment/audit.md:361
new_findings.finding: The shrink-only ratchet on ignored book blocks matches only fences at column 0. An indented fence (inside a list item, which rustdoc still treats as a code block) escapes both the ignore count and the untagged-block check. audit.md:361 is such a `rust,ignore` block, added 2026-10-29 (44ddf59), compiled by nothing and not in .book-ignore-baseline.
new_findings.scenario: Any new snippet that does not compile can be hidden from the ratchet by indenting it under a bullet; the 'every other Rust block in the book is compiled' claim (.book-ignore-baseline header) is already false.

new_findings.finding: 'TLS verification is the library's, against its bundled roots, with no way to turn it off here.' Since 57f034e the library's default (crates/a2a-protocol-client/src/tls.rs:100, :217-225) also trusts `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR` for JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON and WebSocket; gRPC uses tonic's webpki roots only (client Cargo.toml:72), so it does not.
new_findings.scenario: An operator with a private CA does not learn from the CLI README that `SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/ca.pem a2a send https://internal-agent ...` works over the HTTP bindings, and does not learn that `--binding grpc` will still fail.

new_findings.finding: When a release section exceeds 120,000 characters the GitHub release body keeps only '### (Known Limitations|Breaking Changes|Deprecated|Security)' and drops the preamble and '### Behaviour Changes' - the section where 0.15.1 put its two upgrade-relevant changes.
new_findings.scenario: A large release (0.15.0 was 289 KB; [Unreleased] is already 74 KB) carries a runtime behaviour change; adopters reading the GitHub release page never see it.

new_findings.finding: Dependency snippets on main say `a2a-protocol-sdk = "0.16"` / `version = "0.16"` since 476fe03 (2026-10-30), but 0.16.0 is not released (CITATION.cff:17 still 0.15.1, CHANGELOG has only [Unreleased] above [0.15.1]).
new_findings.scenario: Someone copying the Quick Start from the GitHub README on main gets 'failed to select a version for the requirement `a2a-protocol-sdk = "^0.16"`' until 0.16.0 is published. The book site root is the latest release's book (docs.yml header), so only the GitHub view is affected.
